question: What makes an abortion procedure classified as "unsafe"?

options.A: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.B: A legal termination performed in a fully equipped hospital
options.C: A procedure done by unskilled persons or in poor medical environments
options.D: Any abortion that requires the use of surgical instruments

explanation: You've got this! An abortion is unsafe if it's carried out by people without proper training or in places that lack basic medical standards. Keeping patients safe means knowing the difference. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h1)

question: What is a major ethical worry when healthcare services are driven mainly by private profit?

options.A: Eliminating all forms of administrative paperwork across clinical departments
options.B: Prioritizing profitable treatments over care for vulnerable or low-income patients
options.C: Forcing nurses to work longer hours without any form of compensation
options.D: Preventing the government from inspecting hospital financial records

explanation: When money is the main goal, private businesses might focus only on lucrative services and neglect everyday patients who can't afford to pay much. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h6)

question: How does strong teamwork across hospital departments act as a safety net for patients?

options.A: Multiple professionals cross-check information to catch mistakes early
options.B: It guarantees that doctors handle all tasks without nursing help
options.C: It removes all documentation requirements from the nursing shift
options.D: It ensures that patients never need to take any medications

explanation: Fantastic! When departments work closely together, staff watch out for each other and catch little errors before they ever reach the patient. [learn more](GST321_U1_T12#GST321_U1_T12_h6)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand nutrient quantification?

options.A: To measure the physical weight of a patient daily
options.B: To determine the manufacturing date of packaged food items
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of hospital meals
options.D: To accurately evaluate dietary adequacy and plan patient care

explanation: Spotting what's lacking or in excess helps you build a killer care plan for your patients. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T005#GNS227_U4_T005_h1)

question: In a life-threatening poisoning emergency, which route of administration is generally preferred for antidotes?

options.A: Intravenous
options.B: Transdermal
options.C: Subcutaneous
options.D: Rectal suppository

explanation: The IV route puts the antidote straight into the bloodstream so it can start working almost immediately when every second counts. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is a clear example of non-verbal communication?

options.A: Medical terminology
options.B: Written care plans
options.C: Facial expressions
options.D: Spoken explanations

explanation: Correct! Smiles, frowns, and posture speak volumes without you ever opening your mouth. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why is it wonderful for Nigerian nurses to recommend local soups like ugwu and egusi during nutrition talks?

options.A: They are affordable, culturally familiar, and rich in essential nutrients
options.B: They are the only foods allowed by traditional customs during pregnancy
options.C: They replace the need for antenatal clinic attendance
options.D: They completely eliminate the risk of gestational high blood pressure

explanation: Our local soups are packed with vitamins, iron, and good fats! They are easy to find, pocket-friendly, and nourishing. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h6)

question: On a partograph, what does crossing the action line mean for the healthcare team?

options.A: Midwives should wait four more hours
options.B: Immediate medical intervention is required
options.C: The patient is ready for spontaneous delivery
options.D: Labour is progressing at a normal rate

explanation: You've got this! The action line is a clear warning sign that labour is taking longer than expected. It tells us we need to step in and help the mother right away. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h1)

question: Which inventory rule ensures that medicines closer to their expiration date are used first?

options.A: Most-Expensive, First-Used
options.B: First-Expired, First-Out
options.C: Random-Selection Method
options.D: First-In, Last-Out

explanation: Correct! FEFO (First-Expired, First-Out) helps prevent waste and patient risk by making sure older stock gets used before new deliveries. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which type of dietary fiber is especially important to include in the daily meals of older adults?

options.A: Low-residue fiber to completely eliminate bowel movements
options.B: Synthetic fiber powders to speed up stomach emptying
options.C: Animal-derived fiber to build stronger intestinal walls
options.D: High-fiber foods to prevent chronic constipation

explanation: Well done! Because bowel movements tend to slow down with age, fiber is a simple superhero for adding bulk and preventing painful constipation. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T014#GNS227_U2_T014_h2)

question: What causes that unpleasant smell in some gas?

options.A: Sulfur compounds produced by specific gut bacteria
options.B: The breakdown of proteins by liver enzymes
options.C: High levels of pure oxygen from swallowed air
options.D: Undigested stomach acid reaching the rectum

explanation: Certain helpful (and smelly!) bacteria release tiny amounts of sulfur when they break down food. Totally normal body process! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h2)

question: Where do ectopic pregnancies most frequently happen?

options.A: The endocervical canal
options.B: The abdominal cavity
options.C: The urinary bladder
options.D: The fallopian tube

explanation: Correct! Most ectopic pregnancies get stuck in the fallopian tube because the embryo implants on its way down to the uterus. Excellent clinical recall! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T2#GNS121_U6_T2_h6)

question: A mother brings her healthy 14-week-old infant to the primary health clinic. Which group of vaccines is due for this visit?

options.A: BCG, OPV zero, and Hepatitis B birth dose
options.B: Measles first dose and Yellow Fever vaccine
options.C: Rotavirus first dose and Pentavalent first dose
options.D: Pentavalent third dose, OPV 3, IPV, and PCV 3

explanation: At 14 weeks, infants receive the third doses of Pentavalent, OPV, and PCV, along with the first dose of Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV). [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h3)

question: What legal idea lets a patient sue a hospital for a contractor's mistake because the hospital made it look like the worker was their staff?

options.A: Apparent agency
options.B: Respondeat superior
options.C: Stare decisis
options.D: Habeas corpus

explanation: 'Apparent agency' happens when the hospital's setup leads a patient to reasonably believe a contractor is a regular staff member. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h5)

question: If a local government wants to reduce rabies cases in humans, what should they prioritize first?

options.A: Draining all local ponds and slow-moving irrigation streams
options.B: Conducting a mass vaccination campaign for domestic dogs
options.C: Providing free insecticide-treated nets to market traders
options.D: Issuing strict travel bans on all livestock transport vehicles

explanation: Brilliant! Since dogs are the main carrier of rabies, vaccinating them directly protects us from exposure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why are generic drugs generally much more affordable than brand name drugs?

options.A: The government subsidizes all generic manufacturing costs in local factories
options.B: Generic medications are manufactured in smaller quantities than brand drugs
options.C: Generic drugs use lower quality active chemicals to reduce production expenses
options.D: Makers of generic drugs do not carry the original research and marketing costs

explanation: Developing a new drug takes billions in research and advertising. Generic makers skip those initial costs, which is why their prices are much friendlier to patients' pockets. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T8#GNS125_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why does eating a high-protein diet often help people naturally eat fewer calories overall?

options.A: It increases feelings of fullness and satiety
options.B: It completely blocks the absorption of dietary fats
options.C: It lowers the body temperature during digestion
options.D: It speeds up the removal of water weight

explanation: Protein takes longer to digest and sends fullness signals to your brain. This naturally keeps hunger at bay so you don't feel the need to overeat! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h1)

question: When do you need to run a quality control check with liquid control solution?

options.A: Only when the patient asks
options.B: When opening a new container of test strips
options.C: Once every hour
options.D: After every single patient test

explanation: Whenever you crack open a new batch of strips, run a control test to make sure your meter and the new strips agree. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h7)

question: The spinothalamic tract is famous for carrying which type of sensory information to the brain?

options.A: Fine touch and vibration
options.B: Conscious motor commands
options.C: Pain and temperature
options.D: Involuntary heart rate signals

explanation: Whenever you touch something hot or feel a sharp pinch, the spinothalamic tract is the main highway rushing that pain and temperature info up to your brain! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T16#GNS211_U3_T16_h3)

question: Why do nurses check out the living space during a home health visit?

options.A: To evaluate the market value of the family property for billing
options.B: To determine if the patient qualifies for government housing grants
options.C: To check if the patient's physical needs and living space safely match
options.D: To ensure family members are qualified to write medical prescriptions

explanation: You got it! We inspect the home to make sure it is safe and supportive for the patient's recovery without hidden hazards. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h1)

question: Which global region currently has the highest number of maternal deaths?

options.A: North America
options.B: Southeast Asia
options.C: Sub-Saharan Africa
options.D: Western Europe

explanation: As future Nigerian nurses, knowing our local context is key. Sub-Saharan Africa bears the heaviest load of maternal mortality, making our work so important. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T001#GNS226_U1_T001_h2)

question: Under Nigerian law, when is an abortion legally allowed?

options.A: Whenever requested by the male partner or husband
options.B: Only when necessary to save the life of the pregnant woman
options.C: In all cases involving financial hardship or unemployment
options.D: Whenever the woman decides she is not ready for a child

explanation: Spot on. Nigerian law is quite strict and generally permits termination only if the mother's life is in direct danger. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard nursing check before a vasectomy?

options.A: Scheduling a mandatory prostate biopsy
options.B: Checking for active local skin infections
options.C: Screening for permanent reproductive intent
options.D: Evaluating bleeding history and anticoagulant use

explanation: That's right! A prostate biopsy checks for cancer and has nothing to do with routine preparation for a vasectomy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h2)

question: A patient sends a photo of a swollen foot via WhatsApp for a nurse to check later. What type of communication is this?

options.A: Asynchronous delivery
options.B: Synchronous delivery
options.C: Direct ward admission
options.D: Emergency triage

explanation: Exactly! When you send a message or photo to be reviewed later without a live conversation happening right then, it is called asynchronous (or store-and-forward) communication. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h3)

question: A 15-year-old first-time pregnant mother at 36 weeks comes in with a severe headache, blurry vision, and high blood pressure. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Acute gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.C: Chronic adult migraine headaches
options.D: Normal physiological changes of late pregnancy

explanation: Teenage mothers have a higher risk of high blood pressure disorders during pregnancy, which often show up as severe headaches, vision changes, and high BP readings. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h3)

question: Why don't we use the intraarterial route for everyday medications like regular IVs?

options.A: Intravenous medications are always cheaper to manufacture
options.B: Arteries have no blood flow once a needle enters them
options.C: High arterial pressure makes access and maintenance complex and risky
options.D: Drugs given this way are instantly destroyed by liver enzymes

explanation: Arteries pump blood at a much higher pressure than veins! This makes them tricky to manage and prone to serious bleeding, so we save them for special situations. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T13#GNS125_U3_T13_h1)

question: A community nurse visits a stroke survivor weekly to check skin integrity and assist with arm exercises. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Primordial prevention
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: Helping an existing stroke patient recover movement and prevent complications like bedsores is tertiary care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h4)

question: What can a patient usually eat right after a normal, uncomplicated sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: Return to their normal diet right away
options.B: Clear broths only for three days
options.C: Nothing by mouth for 24 hours
options.D: High-fat dairy to coat the stomach

explanation: You nailed it! Unless biopsies or other special steps were taken, patients can jump right back into eating normally. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h7)

question: According to the healthy plate method, what portion of a meal should be fruits and vegetables?

options.A: The entire plate
options.B: One-quarter
options.C: Three-quarters
options.D: One-half

explanation: Filling half the plate with colorful fruits and veggies is a quick, easy rule to make sure a meal is full of fiber and vitamins. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h4)

question: Which blood lab results would you expect to see if a patient's kidneys are suddenly failing?

options.A: Zero detectable sodium ions in blood plasma
options.B: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
options.C: Lowered levels of circulating metabolic waste products
options.D: High concentrations of plasma red blood cells

explanation: Spot on! When the kidneys aren't filtering well, waste products like creatinine and urea build up quickly in the blood. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T6#GNS121_U2_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary reason for maintaining strict aseptic technique during an intrathecal procedure?

options.A: Hospital regulations require sterile gear for all injections
options.B: Bacteria will instantly neutralize any local anesthetic injected
options.C: The central nervous system is highly susceptible to severe infections like meningitis
options.D: Skin flora can cause immediate chemical burns inside the spinal canal

explanation: The central nervous system has limited immune defenses, making introduction of pathogens via unsterile technique catastrophic. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why do nurses refer to pain as the 'fifth vital sign'?

options.A: It directly calculates the exact heart rate of the patient.
options.B: It can be measured using an automated cuff machine.
options.C: It must be checked and recorded alongside standard vital signs.
options.D: It is only relevant during surgical procedures.

explanation: Calling pain the fifth vital sign reminds us to assess and document it just as regularly as temperature or blood pressure. Great job keeping your clinical habits sharp! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is a great advocacy action a nurse can take to support community inclusion?

options.A: Encouraging patients to remain indoors to avoid public ridicule
options.B: Focusing exclusively on medication adherence during home visits
options.C: Educating local leaders and connecting families with welfare resources
options.D: Restricting community nursing visits to clinic grounds only

explanation: You've got it! Nurses act as wonderful bridges by teaching the community and linking families to helpful social resources. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T11#GNS225_U5_T11_h6)

question: Why is checking pregnancy status crucial before giving certain antiprotozoal drugs?

options.A: Pregnant women do not absorb any active ingredients from oral tablets
options.B: Pregnancy completely destroys the ability of the liver to metabolize drugs
options.C: Antimalarial drugs cause instant miscarriage in all trimesters
options.D: Many antiprotozoal agents are teratogenic and contraindicated in early pregnancy

explanation: Brilliant! Some antiprotozoal drugs can harm fetal development, making a pregnancy check an essential safety step. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T5#GNS223_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why is monitoring serum albumin and prealbumin important for these patients?

options.A: They tell the doctor if the patient has a bacterial infection
options.B: They show whether the patient is drinking enough water every day
options.C: They help track the body's protein status and detect malnutrition early
options.D: They measure the exact amount of urine produced each hour

explanation: Blood protein levels give healthcare providers an objective look at how well the patient is tolerating the dietary restriction. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h5)

question: What happens to a hospital's safety culture when management ignores staff reports and refuses to fix staff shortages?

options.A: Nurses become more efficient and independent
options.B: The safety culture erodes and trust breaks down
options.C: Staff morale improves and errors decrease
options.D: Patient satisfaction scores increase rapidly

explanation: When leaders turn a blind eye to feedback, nurses stop reporting issues, and trust between the staff and management quickly falls apart. [learn more](GST319_U6_T6#GST319_U6_T6_h6)

question: A patient is worried about using modern contraceptives because of her religion. As a nurse, what is the best way to respond?

options.A: Provide respectful, non-judgmental counseling that acknowledges her values
options.B: Report her concerns to the hospital administration immediately
options.C: Tell her that her religious beliefs are outdated and incorrect
options.D: Refuse to discuss any options other than surgical sterilization

explanation: Always meet patients where they are! Good nurses respect personal values and give compassionate, supportive guidance without judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h6)

question: What is the primary cause of neonatal tetanus?

options.A: Severe dehydration during the first week of life
options.B: Congenital weakness of the newborn immune system
options.C: A viral infection passed through breast milk
options.D: A neurotoxin produced by Clostridium tetani

explanation: You got this! Neonatal tetanus happens when a powerful toxin released by the bacterium Clostridium tetani attacks a baby's nervous system. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h1)

question: How does severe scarring from past salpingitis increase the risk of an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Fibrous bands force the ovaries to release eggs directly into the peritoneal cavity
options.B: Scar tissue blocks the fertilized egg from traveling down to the uterus, causing it to implant in the tube
options.C: Adhesions destroy all hormonal production needed to support a normal pregnancy
options.D: Scars cause the uterus to shrink so much that eggs refuse to enter it

explanation: When scar tissue narrows or blocks the tube, a fertilized egg gets stuck and has to try to grow right there in the tube instead of the uterus. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h8)

question: In community nursing, how do we best describe a "community"?

options.A: A single hospital ward with patients and staff
options.B: A collection of medical doctors working in one clinic
options.C: Every person living within a country's capital city
options.D: A group of people sharing values, interests, or geography

explanation: Spot on! Think of a community as people connected by bonds, shared spaces, or common goals—not just four hospital walls. You're getting the hang of this! [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why must nurses tailor assessment tools to fit a degenerative patient's physical limits?

options.A: To make the test results legally binding in a court of law
options.B: To eliminate the need for family members to be present
options.C: To ensure the patient does not get tired or frustrated during testing
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing paper questionnaires

explanation: If a patient is exhausted, test scores won't show their true ability. Matching their energy levels keeps the assessment accurate and stress-free. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T18#GNS222_U4_T18_h3)

question: What is a major duty of a healthcare social worker?

options.A: Connecting patients with financial aid and community resources
options.B: Administering daily intravenous antibiotics
options.C: Designing physical exercise routines for stroke recovery
options.D: Performing physical examinations and diagnosing illnesses

explanation: Social workers step in to solve non-medical worries, such as finding financial support, housing, or community help for older patients. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T7#GNS321_U3_T7_h5)

question: How can a poor attitude from healthcare workers negatively impact immunization rates?

options.A: It automatically alters the chemical composition of the vaccines
options.B: Caregivers may avoid returning to the clinic to escape mistreatment
options.C: It causes the government to shut down the primary health center
options.D: It forces clinics to increase the price of immunization services

explanation: Exactly! Rude or harsh behavior from clinic staff pushes parents away and stops them from completing their children's shots. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T69#GNS214_U1_T69_h7)

question: What is a common way survivors of gender-based violence initially present in a clinic?

options.A: By demanding a police officer upon walking through the door
options.B: With vague, chronic complaints and unexplained physical symptoms
options.C: By immediately handing the nurse a written confession of abuse
options.D: With completely normal physical and mental health screenings

explanation: Fear and stigma often prevent immediate disclosure, leading survivors to seek care for headaches, body pain, or anxiety instead. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core component of a standard cardiac rehabilitation program?

options.A: Nutritional counseling and diet advice
options.B: High-dose intravenous chemotherapy
options.C: Supervised physical exercise training
options.D: Education on quitting cigarette smoking

explanation: Chemotherapy treats cancer, not coronary artery disease; cardiac rehab focuses on exercise, nutrition, and lifestyle changes. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h9)

question: A nurse places a naked newborn onto a cold metal scale, making the baby lose body heat. What is this specific type of heat loss called?

options.A: Conduction
options.B: Evaporation
options.C: Convection
options.D: Radiation

explanation: Think of Conduction as direct contact. When a baby touches a cooler solid surface directly, heat transfers right out of them. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h4)

question: What is the main job of a bin card attached to a storage shelf?

options.A: To give instructions on treating needle stick injuries
options.B: To advertise the brand name of the syringe maker
options.C: To show a running balance of stock movements in real time
options.D: To list phone numbers of delivery drivers

explanation: Well done! A bin card acts as a quick ledger right at the shelf, tracking every item added or taken away. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of innovative 'small-house' models in modern nursing care?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any professional healthcare oversight
options.B: To lower building construction costs by using temporary tents
options.C: To break large, sterile institutions down into homelike residential units
options.D: To reduce the total number of older adults requiring assistance worldwide

explanation: Small-house models ditch the long, intimidating hospital hallways and replace them with cozy, home-style spaces where residents can build genuine community connections. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h6)

question: What does the term 'bioavailability' mean when studying nutrition?

options.A: The expiration date stamped on a packaged food item
options.B: The speed at which bacteria break down food in the large intestine
options.C: The fraction of an ingested nutrient that enters the bloodstream and becomes active
options.D: The total percentage of water found inside a raw vegetable

explanation: Exactly right! Bioavailability simply means how much of the nutrient successfully makes it past your gut and into your bloodstream to go to work. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h3)

question: What do we mean by environmental factors in education?

options.A: External conditions and influences shaping the educational experience
options.B: Strictly the financial cost of attending a nursing program
options.C: Only the physical temperature inside a traditional classroom
options.D: The genetic makeup and natural intelligence of the student

explanation: Environmental factors cover all outside elements that impact how you learn, from your physical surroundings to your support systems. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U8_T9#GST321_U8_T9_h1)

question: How do adsorbent drugs help ease diarrhoea symptoms?

options.A: They bind to toxins and fluid on their surface
options.B: They increase blood flow to the intestinal lining
options.C: They paralyze the nerves of the large intestine
options.D: They stimulate the production of healthy gut bacteria

explanation: Think of adsorbents like a sponge in the gut—they grab onto bad toxins and extra liquid, carrying them safely out in the stool. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which nutrient class serves as the body's most rapid and preferred energy source?

options.A: Vitamins
options.B: Carbohydrates
options.C: Minerals
options.D: Proteins

explanation: Carbohydrates break down quickly into glucose, which is the body and brain's favorite fuel for immediate energy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h2)

question: Which nursing action best describes a promotive reproductive health service?

options.A: Suturing a perineal tear following a normal vaginal delivery
options.B: Performing a manual vacuum aspiration for an incomplete miscarriage
options.C: Leading a community health talk on proper menstrual hygiene
options.D: Prescribing antibiotics for a confirmed pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Promotive services involve general health education and encouraging positive wellness practices rather than treating active disease. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which practice should nurses avoid when handling used injection needles?

options.A: Activating the safety device
options.B: Dropping it straight into a bin
options.C: Carrying it in a dedicated tray
options.D: Recapping the needle by hand

explanation: Recapping needles by hand is a major cause of accidental needlestick injuries and should never be done. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: Which body fluid is usually NOT covered under standard precautions?

options.A: Vomitus
options.B: Saliva
options.C: Sweat
options.D: Urine

explanation: Great try! Sweat doesn't carry bloodborne infections, so unless there is visible blood in it, standard precautions don't apply to it. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h1)

question: What is the key sign that an abortion procedure is unsafe?

options.A: Done using standard medical pills prescribed by a doctor
options.B: Conducted inside a registered tertiary hospital facility
options.C: Performed strictly within the first four weeks of gestation
options.D: Performed by untrained persons or in unhygienic environments

explanation: Correct! Unsafe procedures usually happen in dirty places or are done by people without proper medical training. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h2)

question: How do tight budgets usually affect a clinical research study?

options.A: They automatically improve the accuracy of patient records
options.B: They limit sample sizes and shorten follow-up periods
options.C: They make patients more willing to take experimental drugs
options.D: They eliminate the need for ethical board review

explanation: Exactly! Without enough funding, researchers simply cannot afford to track as many people or follow them for very long. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T2#GNS217_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the very first thing you must do if a patient shows signs of an idiosyncratic drug reaction?

options.A: Stop the medication immediately
options.B: Wait forty minutes to see if it passes
options.C: Give a double dose of antihistamines
options.D: Increase the intravenous fluid rate

explanation: Safety first! Always stop the trigger drug right away to keep things from getting worse. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T7#GNS125_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why do animal hookworm larvae cause wandering red lines on human skin instead of a deeper infection?

options.A: Because humans are accidental dead-end hosts where the larvae cannot complete their life cycle
options.B: Because topical soaps paralyze the nervous system of the parasites immediately
options.C: Because human white blood cells instantly freeze the larvae in place under the skin
options.D: Because the larvae lack the physical strength to bite through muscle fascia

explanation: Since humans aren't their normal hosts, the larvae get confused and wander aimlessly in the top layers of the skin. Makes sense when you picture it! [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h3)

question: At 36 weeks, a mum is scheduled for surgery. Why must the medical team act quickly when securing her airway?

options.A: Reduced functional residual capacity leads to rapid drops in oxygen levels
options.B: Total lung capacity drops to zero once the patient lies flat
options.C: High progesterone completely paralyzes the swallow reflex instantly
options.D: The widened rib cage makes the vocal cords impossible to visualize

explanation: Mums have smaller air reserves late in pregnancy, meaning their oxygen levels can drop quicker during procedures. Excellent clinical insight! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T3#GNS121_U7_T3_h3)

question: Why is the formation of a dense fibrin mesh essential for wound healing?

question: What was a major benefit when hospital-based home care programs first started?

question: A newly delivered mother needs support with lochia assessment and breastfeeding. Which midwife responsibility applies here?

question: What is the main job of a Nurse Principal Investigator?

question: What is the main difference between good (appropriate) polypharmacy and bad (problematic) polypharmacy?

question: When lifestyle changes don't quite cut it, what type of medication is usually recommended first for pregnancy heartburn?

question: Why is asking about family bleeding history so important before a circumcision?

question: How are medical services primarily distributed in a free market economy?

question: What does MBO stand for in healthcare management?

question: What is the main difference between nutrition and dietetics?

options.A: Nutrition applies only to sick patients, while dietetics applies to healthy people
options.B: Dietetics focuses only on food production, while nutrition focuses on medicine
options.C: Nutrition is the study of food, while dietetics is how we apply it to help people
options.D: There is no difference and the two terms mean the exact same thing

explanation: Think of nutrition as the science behind food, and dietetics as putting that science into action for patient care. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T001#GNS227_U4_T001_h2)

question: When should a community health nurse clean and disinfect a measuring tape?

options.A: Only when it looks visibly dirty
options.B: Once a month during equipment audit
options.C: At the end of each working week
options.D: After every single client use

explanation: Wiping the tape after every patient prevents the spread of skin infections and pathogens between community members. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h6)

question: Why is writing down complete notes about pain care so important for nurses?

options.A: It replaces the need to talk directly with the patient.
options.B: It is only required for legal protection during lawsuits.
options.C: It ensures safe continuity of care and evaluates if treatment worked.
options.D: It allows the hospital to bill insurance companies faster.

explanation: Clear notes help the whole healthcare team see what worked, keep the patient safe, and coordinate the next steps smoothly. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of taking and handing over on the ward?

options.A: To transfer patient care responsibilities safely between shifts
options.B: To replace formal written patient medical records completely
options.C: To give nurses a chance to socialise before starting work
options.D: To allow doctors to check if nurses are doing their jobs

explanation: Handover makes sure that important care details move securely from the outgoing nurse to the incoming one, so no patient is left unprotected! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h1)

question: What gets squeezed flat against the tunica albuginea to trap blood inside the penis?

options.A: Subtunical venules
options.B: Dorsal nerve fibers
options.C: Cavernous arteries
options.D: Urethral glands

explanation: You're getting the hang of this! As the internal spaces fill up, they press the tiny drainage veins (venules) flat so blood cannot escape. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T4#GNS121_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is the final step after completing a community situation analysis?

options.A: Closing down the primary health center for renovations
options.B: Translating the findings into an actionable health plan
options.C: Waiting for another NGO to come and do the work
options.D: Destroying all survey papers to protect patient privacy

explanation: The entire purpose of gathering and analyzing situation data is to guide practical healthcare planning and intervention. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h7)

question: Why do many men often spread STIs without even knowing they have them?

options.A: Male anatomy completely blocks bacterial growth
options.B: Common pathogens only survive inside female tissues
options.C: Many infected men show no early symptoms at all
options.D: Routine blood tests always cure the infection early

explanation: It's tricky! Many guys feel completely healthy and normal while carrying an infection, which is why education and screening are so important. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why do nurse researchers love using checklists instead of messy, freehand notes?

options.A: Checklists reduce missed details and ensure consistency
options.B: Checklists completely eliminate the need for human observers
options.C: Checklists are the only tool allowed by ethical boards
options.D: Checklists take no time at all to design or implement

explanation: Busy hospital shifts can be chaotic. A good checklist keeps your data uniform and stops you from forgetting important details! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T23#GNS224_U1_T23_h1)

question: Which of these action verbs should you avoid in a research objective because it is too vague?

options.A: To appreciate
options.B: To measure
options.C: To identify
options.D: To compare

explanation: Words like 'appreciate' or 'understand' are feelings—they are too subjective and impossible to measure accurately in a study. Stick to concrete verbs! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why is fast teamwork among healthcare staff so essential when managing GI complications?

options.A: Conditions can deteriorate into life-threatening emergencies very quickly
options.B: Nurses are not allowed to touch patients without a doctor present
options.C: Medical staff must share paperwork equally among themselves
options.D: Collaborative care guarantees that surgery will never be needed

explanation: You got it! Emergencies like bowel tears or massive bleeding move fast, meaning the team has to act together instantly to keep the patient safe. Teamwork makes the dream work in nursing! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h8)

question: A nurse records a patient's exact weight in kilograms. What type of measurement scale is this?

options.A: Nominal scale
options.B: Interval scale
options.C: Ordinal scale
options.D: Ratio scale

explanation: Weight is measured on a ratio scale because it has equal intervals and a true zero point where zero kilograms means an absolute absence of weight. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h2)

question: When would you choose an intramuscular injection instead of giving pills by mouth?

options.A: When the patient cannot take oral medications
options.B: When the patient wants to avoid any skin punctures
options.C: When the medication needs to work over a full week
options.D: When the drug is completely harmless to the stomach

explanation: Spot on! If a patient is vomiting or unable to swallow, going through the muscle is a safe and reliable backup plan. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T3#GNS122_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why do doctors prescribe antidiabetic medications for patients with diabetes mellitus?

options.A: To restore normal metabolic balance and lower blood sugar
options.B: To permanently replace the need for dietary modifications
options.C: To stimulate the continuous release of stored glucagon
options.D: To completely cure the underlying pancreatic disease

explanation: You got it! These drugs help keep blood glucose in check to prevent long-term complications, even though they aren't a permanent cure on their own. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h1)

question: Why is the left anterior descending (LAD) artery famously called the widow-maker?

options.A: It carries deoxygenated blood back to the lungs.
options.B: It is the longest vein in the human heart.
options.C: It supplies blood to the major pumping walls of the left ventricle.
options.D: It controls the electrical rhythm of the heart valves.

explanation: Spot on! The LAD feeds the thick, heavy-duty walls of the left ventricle. If it gets blocked, the heart's main pumping power is severely crippled. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T10#GNS111_U2_T10_h1)

question: A farmer comes to the clinic drooling, crying watery tears, and having muscle twitching after spraying his crops. Which type of chemical is most likely to blame?

options.A: Inert plastic polymers
options.B: Heavy metal lead
options.C: Organophosphate pesticides
options.D: Strong household acids

explanation: Well done! Organophosphates overstimulate the nervous system by blocking an enzyme called acetylcholinesterase. This creates those classic 'wet' signs like drooling, excessive tearing, and twitching. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T8#GNS215_U5_T8_h2)

question: What is the main job of the tiny hair-like cilia in your airways?

options.A: Absorb oxygen directly from inhaled air
options.B: Produce special chemicals to break down cell walls
options.C: Secrete thick mucus to trap foreign particles
options.D: Sweep trapped dust and germs upward and away from the lungs

explanation: Cilia use gentle, wave-like motions to push mucus and dirt up and out of your breathing tubes, keeping your lungs clean. [learn more](GST114_U4_T4#GST114_U4_T4_h2)

question: A patient has muffled heart sounds and a sudden blood pressure crash after an intracardiac injection. What is happening?

options.A: Normal recovery
options.B: A urinary tract infection
options.C: Cardiac tamponade
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: Spot on! Blood pooling inside the sac around the heart dampens the heart sounds and stops the heart from filling with blood, crashing the blood pressure. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T14#GNS125_U3_T14_h7)

question: Why has feeding advice for mums with HIV improved so much in recent years?

options.A: Formula milk has been completely banned globally
options.B: Antiretroviral therapy has made safe breastfeeding possible
options.C: Breast milk no longer contains any active viral particles
options.D: Infants are now naturally immune to the virus at birth

explanation: Modern medicine is amazing! Better drugs lower the viral load significantly, meaning mums can now breastfeed much more safely than in the past. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T12#GNS216_U6_T12_h1)

question: Why does the conjunctiva become easily inflamed during an infection?

options.A: It lacks any form of blood supply
options.B: It is directly exposed to the external environment
options.C: It produces thick, sticky tears
options.D: It contains heavy layers of bone

explanation: Because the conjunctiva lines the exposed outer surface of the eye and inner eyelids, it readily catches dust, germs, and allergens. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h1)

question: What medical term describes how severe or dangerous a disease is when caused by an infectious agent?

options.A: Contagiosity
options.B: Virulence
options.C: Pathogenicity
options.D: Infectivity

explanation: Think of virulence as the 'punch' a germ packs. It tells us how severe or even fatal the resulting disease can be to the host. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T2#GNS313_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why do dry-heat cooking methods create brown crusts and rich flavors on food?

options.A: They use high temperatures that trigger the Maillard reaction on the food surface.
options.B: They rely on water molecules to break down complex sugars into simple starches.
options.C: They add liquid fats that caramelize quickly when exposed to steam.
options.D: They remove all moisture from the food interior before cooking begins.

explanation: When high dry heat hits proteins and sugars on the surface, it causes the famous Maillard reaction—giving us that wonderful roasted aroma and golden crust. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h4)

question: What is the main transmission route for most water-borne pathogens?

options.A: The fecal-oral route
options.B: Skin contact with soil
options.C: Direct airborne droplets
options.D: Mosquito bite vectors

explanation: Water-borne diseases spread when microscopic fecal matter contaminates drinking or food preparation water, which is then swallowed. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h4)

question: At 20 weeks pregnant, a patient's serum creatinine level is 1.0 mg/dL. What does this result suggest?

options.A: Severe maternal dehydration
options.B: Normal kidney function for pregnancy
options.C: Potential underlying renal impairment
options.D: A normal non-pregnant baseline

explanation: Because kidney filtration speeds up during pregnancy, normal creatinine levels actually drop below 1.0 mg/dL. A value of 1.0 mg/dL means the kidneys might not be clearing waste as well as they should right now. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h2)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should check before moving a patient to a chair?

options.A: The color of the patient's room walls
options.B: The brand name of the hospital bed
options.C: The patient's current ability to bear weight
options.D: The exact time the doctor's shift ends

explanation: Always check if the patient can stand or support themselves first! This tells you if you need an extra pair of hands or a mechanical lift. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: Why is vocational training an important part of holistic fistula care?

options.A: It teaches the patient how to use specialized machinery to clean hospital linen
options.B: It helps survivors regain financial independence and rebuild their lives after social stigma
options.C: It acts as a substitute for medical treatment when surgery fails to close the hole
options.D: It trains the patient to perform minor surgical repairs on other women in the village

explanation: Great job! Learning a trade empowers these women economically, helping them bounce back from poverty and isolation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h6)

question: Which type of breathing problem involves a dangerous buildup of carbon dioxide?

options.A: A buildup of carbon dioxide due to poor ventilation
options.B: A sudden drop in oxygen caused by fluid in the alveoli
options.C: High blood pressure inside the arteries of the lungs
options.D: A complete collapse of the lung tissue from air in the chest

explanation: Correct! When a patient isn't moving air in and out well enough (poor ventilation), carbon dioxide gets trapped inside. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T12#GNS213_U2_T12_h2)

question: A patient has an autoimmune condition where their insulin-making cells are destroyed. What lab finding is most likely?

options.A: Dangerously low blood sugar caused by excess hormone release
options.B: Rapid weight gain due to slowed metabolic breakdown
options.C: Elevated blood glucose levels due to a lack of insulin
options.D: Increased water retention and high blood pressure

explanation: Without insulin (hyposecretion), glucose can't easily enter the body's cells to be used for energy. Instead, it builds up in the bloodstream, leading to high blood sugar. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T3#GNS211_U1_T3_h8)

question: Why should nurses check on the emotional well-being of brothers and sisters in a family affected by cerebral palsy?

options.A: Parents usually ignore the affected child to focus entirely on healthy siblings
options.B: Siblings must legally take over financial caregiving once they turn eighteen
options.C: Siblings are at high risk of developing cerebral palsy themselves
options.D: Siblings can experience feelings of neglect, stress, or added responsibilities

explanation: A chronic condition affects the whole household. Siblings often need emotional support to handle changing roles and big feelings. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h7)

question: Why do uterine contractions eventually become weaker during a prolonged, blocked labour?

options.A: The uterine muscle runs out of energy from overworking
options.B: The maternal kidneys start retaining excess fluids
options.C: The placenta stops producing progesterone
options.D: The baby's heartbeat suppresses uterine activity

explanation: Think of the uterus like any other muscle in the body. If it keeps pushing hard against a blockage without a break, it eventually gets exhausted and runs out of energy! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h2)

question: Which part of a feedback loop is responsible for detecting a change in the body?

options.A: Set point
options.B: Receptor
options.C: Effector
options.D: Control center

explanation: Spot on! Receptors act as your body's scouts or sensors, picking up any changes (stimuli) in your internal or external environment. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T7#GNS123_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is an important nursing duty when a pregnant patient is given an antiemetic drug?

options.A: Encourage the patient to stop taking all oral fluids
options.B: Advise the patient to double the dose if nausea returns
options.C: Check fetal heart tones every fifteen minutes around the clock
options.D: Monitor the patient for common side effects like drowsiness

explanation: Many antiemetics make patients sleepy. Keeping an eye on safety and advising them about drowsiness is a key nursing role. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h5)

question: What is a common cause of diarrhea when a patient is receiving tube feeds at home?

options.A: Elevating the bed during the feeding
options.B: Keeping the room temperature too warm
options.C: Infusing the formula too rapidly
options.D: Flushing the tube with plain sterile water

explanation: Correct! Pumping formula too fast overwhelms the gut and frequently causes cramps and diarrhea. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h6)

question: How does the human ear act like a biological transducer?

options.A: It filters out background noise using chemical barriers
options.B: It converts mechanical air vibrations into electrical nerve signals
options.C: It amplifies light waves into visual images in the brain
options.D: It stores sound energy inside the fluid of the middle ear

explanation: Transduction simply means changing one form of energy into another. The ear takes physical sound waves moving through the air and translates them into electrical messages your brain can understand. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why are gentle range-of-motion exercises and turning schedules crucial for residents who cannot move much on their own?

options.A: To speed up the metabolic rate and cure underlying chronic infections
options.B: To prevent secondary complications like contractures and pressure injuries
options.C: To eliminate the need for any nutritional support or dietary supplements
options.D: To guarantee that the resident will never need assistance walking again

explanation: Moving and turning patients keeps their joints flexible and protects their skin from painful pressure sores. Excellent nursing practice! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of food distribution systems?

options.A: Setting international trade tariffs on crops
options.B: Regulating chemical use in commercial farming
options.C: Moving food from farms to consumers
options.D: Determining the retail price of imported meat

explanation: Food distribution is fundamentally about bridging the physical gap between agricultural production sites and the final consumer. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h1)

question: Why should the person who orders hospital supplies be different from the person who approves the payment?

options.A: To ensure that nurses never have to handle administrative paperwork
options.B: To maintain separation of duties and reduce the risk of fraud
options.C: To allow the finance department to dictate clinical patient care
options.D: To make sure orders take longer to process through the system

explanation: Separating these duties creates a safety net. When two different people handle ordering and paying, it greatly reduces the chance of theft or financial mix-ups. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h3)

question: How do non-drug (non-pharmacological) methods help ease a patient's discomfort?

options.A: They permanently destroy local nerve endings
options.B: They chemically replace lost natural endorphins
options.C: They completely cure the underlying disease
options.D: They engage the mind and body to lower stress and pain signals

explanation: You're crushing it! Techniques like distraction, relaxation, and positioning don't just 'distract'—they actually trigger pathways in the nervous system that block pain signals. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h6)

question: A rural health clinic receives proper funding and regularly restocks its shelves. What is the most likely result for mothers in that community?

options.A: Increased reliance on traditional medicine
options.B: Higher travel costs to city hospitals
options.C: Fewer visits to the clinic for routine checkups
options.D: Lower rates of maternal and infant mortality during childbirth

explanation: When local clinics have supplies and trained staff, mothers and babies survive routine complications. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the very first thing you should do when facing an ethical dilemma at a patient's home?

options.A: Ask the family to make the final decision without the patient
options.B: Identify the specific moral principles and facts involved in the conflict
options.C: Ignore the problem and focus only on physical wound care
options.D: Call the police immediately to remove the patient

explanation: You nailed it! Before you can solve a tangled ethical problem, you have to step back, look at the facts, and figure out exactly which values are clashing. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T10#GNS324_U1_T10_h8)

question: Why is little-by-little exposure to radiation dangerous for healthcare workers over time?

options.A: It makes the nurse feel dizzy immediately after entering the room
options.B: It can cause gradual tissue damage and cellular mutations over years
options.C: It weakens the bones within a few minutes of standing nearby
options.D: It instantly heats up the skin and causes severe third-degree burns

explanation: Radiation adds up in the body over your career. That's why wearing your lead shield every single time is so important. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why must nurses check absolute neutrophil counts before giving chemotherapy?

options.A: To measure how fast the kidneys are filtering urine
options.B: To check if the patient has a hidden vitamin deficiency
options.C: To see if the patient is eating enough protein
options.D: To ensure the patient's immune system is strong enough to handle the drug

explanation: Chemo can lower white blood cells, so checking neutrophils first keeps your patient safe from dangerous infections. Safety first, nurse! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which type of topical treatment is best for treating a stubborn, thick, dry patch of skin?

options.A: Aqueous solution
options.B: Ointment
options.C: Lotion
options.D: Gel

explanation: Ointments are oil-based and heavy, making them champs at locking in moisture and softening thick, dry skin. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T12#GNS215_U6_T12_h3)

question: During a routine speculum exam, you notice a red, velvety patch on a patient's cervix. What is your priority action?

options.A: Preparing the patient for emergency surgical removal of the cervix
options.B: Assisting with obtaining a Pap smear and screening tests to rule out dysplasia or infection
options.C: Instructing the patient to avoid all fluid intake for twelve hours
options.D: Administering intravenous antibiotics immediately without testing

explanation: Always prioritize screening! You can't tell what a red patch is just by looking at it, so a Pap smear or swab is necessary to check for infections or abnormal cells. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h5)

question: What is a practical public health strategy used to boost local food availability?

options.A: Encouraging families to stop buying fresh fruits and vegetables
options.B: Increasing taxes on food items sold in urban supermarkets
options.C: Closing down smallholder farms to build larger hospitals
options.D: Establishing community food banks and improving rural roads

explanation: Better roads and food banks help supplies move safely and reach communities that need them most. Excellent practical knowledge! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T021#GNS227_U2_T021_h8)

question: Why do different health workers come together as a team in community health?

options.A: To address complex health and social needs
options.B: To place full control of care on physicians
options.C: To reduce the number of working nurses
options.D: To lower the cost of running hospital wards

explanation: You've got this! Community health involves many overlapping social and physical issues, so different experts team up to tackle them all together. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h1)

question: What is the classic early symptom of Spinal Cord Compression in cancer patients?

options.A: Inability to swallow
options.B: New, persistent back pain
options.C: Sudden visual loss
options.D: Severe chest pain

explanation: Back pain that worsens when lying flat is almost always the earliest warning sign of a tumor pressing on the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h3)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism)?

options.A: A fast and pounding heartbeat
options.B: Shaking hands and muscle tremors
options.C: Intolerance to cold temperatures
options.D: Sudden and unexplained weight loss

explanation: You nailed it! When the metabolism slows down due to low thyroid hormone, patients feel chilly even when everyone else is warm. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T2#GNS222_U2_T2_h4)

question: A nurse wants to know a patient's actual food intake over the past day. Which assessment method is best suited for this?

options.A: A 24-hour dietary recall
options.B: An inpatient surgical biopsy
options.C: A two-week physical exercise log
options.D: A complete genetic blood screening

explanation: The 24-hour dietary recall asks the patient to list all foods and drinks consumed during the previous day to estimate nutrient intake. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h2)

question: How does early Pick's disease usually look different from Alzheimer's disease?

options.A: Alzheimer's disease exclusively affects people under age fifty.
options.B: Alzheimer's disease causes rapid physical paralysis unlike Pick's disease.
options.C: Pick's disease alters behavior and personality first rather than memory.
options.D: Pick's disease begins with severe visual hallucinations.

explanation: You've got this! While Alzheimer's usually attacks memory first, Pick's disease changes how a person acts, talks to others, and handles their emotions right from the start. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why is it important for nurses in Nigeria to ask patients about any traditional herbal remedies they might be taking?

options.A: Traditional herbs are scientifically proven to cure type 1 diabetes permanently
options.B: Herbal products completely replace the need for blood glucose monitoring
options.C: Traditional remedies have no chemical impact on human liver enzymes
options.D: Herbal mixtures can interact with prescribed drugs and cause unexpected blood sugar drops

explanation: Spot on! Many local herbal preparations can unexpectedly drop blood sugar levels, leading to severe hypoglycaemia when mixed with regular diabetes medications. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h7)

question: What should a nurse manager do if evaluation reveals that a newly implemented patient safety plan failed to reduce medication errors?

options.A: Stop collecting data on medication errors entirely
options.B: Immediately fire all nurses working on the affected unit
options.C: Analyze what went wrong, adjust the strategy, and try again
options.D: Pretend the results do not exist and file the report away

explanation: Management planning is a continuous cycle; when a plan falls short, the manager must revise it and adapt. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is the primary advantage of using an ultrasound for genitourinary assessment?

options.A: It requires general anesthesia for every patient
options.B: It provides a biopsy of the kidney tissue automatically
options.C: It does not expose the patient to radiation
options.D: It measures blood pressure inside the renal arteries

explanation: Ultrasound relies on sound waves rather than ionizing radiation, making it a safe diagnostic imaging option. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h5)

question: How does social justice guide a community health nurse during advocacy?

options.A: It drives the nurse to fight for fair access to health resources for everyone
options.B: It requires the nurse to obey hospital management without question
options.C: It forces the nurse to prioritize wealthy patients who pay higher taxes
options.D: It allows the nurse to make medical diagnoses independently

explanation: Well done! Social justice is about fairness—making sure everyone, rich or poor, gets a fair share of healthcare resources to close health gaps. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h2)

question: What usually pushes someone to start a very strict food fad?

options.A: An innate biological need to consume fewer than five hundred calories
options.B: A clinical requirement to study human metabolism in real-time
options.C: A professional obligation to test new commercial food products
options.D: A desire for control and quick solutions to personal anxieties

explanation: When life feels overwhelming, people often use strict food rules to regain a sense of personal control. You're doing amazing! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a hospital budget?

options.A: Hiding financial losses from the external government auditors
options.B: Determining which nurses receive promotions based on seniority
options.C: Planning how expected revenue will be spent over a specific period
options.D: Punishing departments that fail to meet their monthly patient targets

explanation: Think of a budget as your financial roadmap! It helps a hospital map out expected income and plan expenses for a set timeframe. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following is considered a direct source of data for maternal mortality?

options.A: General household census questionnaires
options.B: Retrospective community interviews about sisters
options.C: Hospital admission and delivery registers
options.D: Mathematical models based on neighboring countries

explanation: Hospital registers and civil registration records capture actual events directly as they are documented in health facilities or official registries. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h3)

question: What is a very common challenge when trying to introduce quality improvement in a busy Nigerian ward?

options.A: Staff burnout and resistance to new routines
options.B: Patients demanding too many safety checklists
options.C: An excess of extra nursing staff on every shift
options.D: Doctors writing too many clear care instructions

explanation: So true! When nurses are already tired and overworked from busy shifts, asking them to learn brand new routines can be tough. We have to support each other! [learn more](GST319_U3_T1#GST319_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why do hospitals rely on redundancy (like independent double-checks) for high-alert drugs like insulin?

options.A: To slow down medication administration so nurses take more break time
options.B: To have multiple independent checks catch a mistake before it reaches the patient
options.C: To ensure the pharmacy department always has excess stock on hand
options.D: To increase the paperwork burden and track staff productivity

explanation: Exactly! Redundancy adds a safety net. If one person has a momentary slip, the second independent check is there to catch it. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h6)

question: Which sign tells you an elderly patient with severe diarrhoea is slipping into advanced dehydration?

options.A: Slow, deep breathing with warm, flushed skin
options.B: Dry mucous membranes and delayed capillary refill
options.C: High blood pressure and excessive saliva production
options.D: Increased muscle strength in the lower limbs

explanation: A dry mouth, sticky tongue, and sluggish refill when you press the fingernail mean there just isn't enough fluid circulating in the body anymore. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why do nurses always stress taking birth control pills at the exact same time every single day?

options.B: Enlarged heart valves

question: Why is promoting local food sources so important when you are counseling patients on their diet?
